scope: Read-only diagnosis: immutable 10,000-transition checkpoint; no production source mutations, no training process mutation, and no artificial object motion.
findings: Optimizing the current reward rationally learns flinging: the deterministic throw yields +93.8768 in 0.3 seconds, from rewards +22.3912, +121.4856, -50. Only 1.0550 of 11.2300 radians were accumulated with >=2 finger contacts and <=30 degree axial tilt. 7.0114 radians were accumulated with zero finger contacts.

The 0.2-second endpoint has zero finger contacts and tilt 111.3 degrees yet earns +121.4856. Contact-loss grace and intermittent renewed contact defer the drop signal until step 3. This is objective exploitation, not numerical success misreporting: success is false throughout.

Action units amplify exploration. Initial raw Gaussian std .05 means approximately .0168-.0466 radians of independent joint-target noise, not .05 radians total across the hand. All 10 tested seeds dropped within the 10-second horizon, mean .97 seconds. Reducing raw std to .01 raises mean survival to only 3.95 seconds.

The learned deterministic first target changes by .5058 radians; steps 2 and 3 change by 1.5348 and 1.6020 radians. Forces hit the .7 N m bound; peak joint speed is 13.1481 rad/s and peak object angular speed 69.4610 rad/s.

Slew-limiting the exact same learned deterministic outputs to .02 rad/control-step gives 13.1-second survival and 2.0788 retained radians, with >=2 contacts and <=30-degree tilt for 98.1% of physics samples. This comparison supports incremental action limits without claiming task success.

The supposedly stable initial controls eventually drop at 86.1 seconds, following roughly 86 seconds of retained but slowly slipping grasp. Its nominal discounted time-cost-only value at gamma .995 is -59.34 for 900 steps, worse than an immediate -50 drop. The constant -.3 paper time cost is therefore counterproductive before bootstrap acquires rotation.

Observation channels have very different scales: initial joint positions reach1.19 rad, object position .0704 m, quaternion .9873; the throw yields per-control-step finite-difference joint velocity7.03 rad/s and object velocity1.30 m/s. State normalization may help but is secondary to action/reward mismatch.

recommendations.scope: Bootstrap simulation SAC only; preserve original environment/reward for the paper method.
recommendations.actions: Use a separately documented incremental command mapping: delta-target bounded .02 rad per 0.1-second step; clip target error from measured joint q to .15 rad. Actor mean starts at zero residual; raw std .05 then corresponds to .001 rad target perturbation. Preserve actual previous physical target in the observation so the wrapper is Markov.
recommendations.reward: Account for signed physics-step axial increments. Gate positive increments by >=2 contacts, <=30 degree tilt and bounded hand workspace. Keep all negative increments. Cap only the positive per-control-step total at .1 rad (2 reward units at multiplier20), leave negative totals uncapped. Remove the -.3 bootstrap time cost; retain drop and actual completion penalties/bonuses. Add explicit object position/tilt penalties only if needed and log components.
recommendations.success: Require a full retained physical rotation, not accumulated off-axis or airborne twist followed by reacquisition. Keep an independent conservative qualified-progress accumulator and disclose the bootstrap success criterion.
recommendations.why_asymmetric: Symmetric signed clipping can reward zero-net-angle cycles: slow forward progress accumulates rewards while a fast reverse step pays only the capped negative cost. Gating all signed increments can similarly reward held-forward/unheld-reverse cycles. Gating/capping positive increments only and charging all actual negative twist makes total progress reward <=20 times actual net axial progress.
recommendations.validation: Test command-rate and target-error bounds; adversarial forward/backward reward cycles; zero-contact and excess-tilt rotations; persistence of incremental-action state and qualified-progress state; successful extraction still requires a full physical rotation. Train fresh bootstrap weights and replay because the new action/reward semantics are incompatible with old checkpoints.

artifact: probe_results.json contains the complete 2-ms physical traces for trained, hold, and slew-limited controls. All probes use the unmodified source environment with observation-only finger_contacts instrumentation.

incremental_noise_validation.conclusion: The same raw Gaussian exploration std .05 survives all 10 20-second episodes with bounded incremental control, versus all10 seeds dropping after mean .97seconds with absolute control. This validates initial exploration retention only, not learned rotation success.
